normative.requirement: Expressions inherit Step specialization requirements. Composite and owning-type predicates determine additional structure-owned and behavior-owned specializations; these constraints do not exclude a Step merely because its direction is non-null.

resolved_implementation.direction_boundary: Expression default context roles are independent of direction. FeatureAdapter applies direction == null to its separate bound-value subsetting operation; that does not gate the inherited expression default operation. Receiver-owned valuations/crossing, metadata, conjugation, end and completed lifecycle remain excluded from this bounded consumer.
resolved_implementation.native_dependencies: Generated base names, roles and adapter selectors; handwritten canonical owner predicates, typed navigation, effect composition and transactional physical materialization.

bounded_controls: 960 independent observations across20 expression bindings, four directions, six ownership contexts and two composite flags. Receivers are incomplete/non-end; owners and library targets are supplied completed fixtures. This verifies a contribution component, not the validity of complete callable models or cold resource closure.
disagreements_and_limits: The pinned PDF uses singular subperformance, enclosedPerformance and ownedPerformance names in Step constraints; the pinned Pilot programs use plural subperformances, enclosedPerformances and ownedPerformances. Native contribution controls preserve the imported pinned implementation names; normative agreement on these library roles remains open and must be resolved before full qualification.
Detached/package directed expressions and unspecified invocation/operator targets are boundary controls, not evidence of normative validity.
Direction enum values are validated through imported Ecore contracts. This does not implement argument/result direction validation for a complete model.
FeatureValue ownership is not equivalent to receiver-owned FeatureValue; bound-value algorithms remain a separate dependency.
